decisions.reason: The accelerator program needed little capital investment and was never made a flagship, so dropping it would cost little; its home-page visibility and fit with the firm's ecosystem strategy still tip the decision narrowly toward keeping it.

The CO2-negative bitumen binder was publicly framed as a flagship of the firm's direction and has its own page, so management will attribute slow uptake to a still-maturing market and persist with it.
The infectious waste plant carries heavy development investment, a publicly announced partnership with ERMAFA and flagship status, so withdrawing it would expose the earlier decision and is unlikely.
The mobile mechanical recycling plant sits close to the core WASTX offer and was announced as the latest product on the home page, making it embedded and visibly committed, so it will be kept.
